purpose: Test whether Gaussian sign pairing improves state coverage at fixed32 outputs for the qualified compact500 model. Same weights, guidance, precision, solver and retry cap as compact IID; no reference-informed sampling.
sampling: Logical draw d uses Gaussian index floor(d/2), with positive sign for even d and negative sign for odd d. Decoder noise is fixed at index0. Output slot k retries d=k+32*a for a=0..3; first coarse-valid sample wins, exhausted slots return the original. Same frozen external seed and compact conditioning as baseline.
controls: All48 single-versus-batch controls retain0.2A RMSD/0.99 CA-lDDT limits. All16 positive first draws per family must match the first16 IID raw backbones under these limits and exactly identical coarse validity. Every attempted noise address/sign, failure and selected output retained. Negative draws intentionally differ and remain in all denominators.
analysis: Unchanged48-family state/MD protocol, raw and selected32 separately. Compare against compact IID selected32 and report full MD differences. Sampling quality needs CA lower95% bound>-0.005, validity difference>=-0.01 and coverage difference>=0. Follow up a diversity gain only if coverage gain>=0.1 with positive lower95% bound. No pairing, temperature, sample-count or seed-search grid. Native quality versus original and compact IID is required first.
resources: One RTX,15minutes,780second worker cap; automatic artifact audit and CPU scoring. Existing baseline reused after exact checkpoint/seed/native lineage checks. <=8 own running+pending GPUs;15UTC deadline; locked tests remain unscored.
